segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Valsa Williams with the Midday News.
With the headlines, 12th Briggs Parliamentary Forum begins in New Delhi to discuss regional
conflicts, economic instability, terrorism and climate change. Prime Minister Narendra
Modi congratulates Brazilian President Dula da Silva on his election victory, expresses
his commitment to deepen multifaceted India-Brasil strategic partnership.
Cyclone Ornab likely to intensify into very severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow, with gusty
winds up to 140 km per hour, IMD predicts heavy to extremely heavy rainfall at isolated
places in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
Global oil prices dip over 1 percent, Brent crude continues to hover at $115 per barrel
and week-long vigilance awareness begins from today to achieve corruption-free society.
Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla has said
Parliament can play an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and trust,
reducing international tensions and finding peaceful solutions to global challenges.
Addressing the inaugural session of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi,
Mr Birla highlighted challenges such as regional conflicts,
conflicts, wars, economic instability, trade tensions, terrorism, and climate change.
He stressed the need for solutions that improve citizens' lives and contribute to a more inclusive
and peaceful world.
The true strength of parliamentary diplomacy lies in our ability to incorporate a democratic
perspective into international relations, while respecting each other's sovereignty
and to translate mutual understanding, trust, and dialogue fostered through shared experiences
and collective actions into concrete cooperation.
Mr Birla expressed confidence that the deliberations at this forum will give a new direction to
mutual trust and cooperation, and further strengthen their shared commitment to people-centric
development.
He said, together, this forum will build a parliamentary partnership that creates new
opportunities for peace, prosperity, and sustainable development, and contributes
to fulfilling the aspirations of the people.
Our parliaments are dynamic institutions that must continuously adapt to public expectations,
embrace innovation in their operational processes, and strengthen the traditions of consensus,
transparency, and accountability.
In a parliamentary context, innovation entails making democratic institutions more effective.
Such institutions must be transparent, participatory, and people-centric, and actively adopt new
ideas and novel working methods.
Describing India as the mother of democracy, Mr. Birla highlighted that India's democratic
strength lies in dialogue, diversity of opinions and mutual respect.
He noted that through this democratic foundation, India is steadily advancing on its development
journey.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi also attended the inaugural session of the 12th Bricks Parliamentary
Forum at the Central Hall, Samvidhan Southern Parliament House.
Mr Modi also met the leaders of the visiting delegations.
Earlier, Lok Sabha Speaker Ombilah welcomed the leaders of the parliamentary delegation
of 11 BRICS member countries and 10 partner countries.
The two-day event will conclude tomorrow.
The theme of the two-day event is fostering parliaments for people-centric development.
11 BRICS member countries and 10 partner countries have been invited for the event.
First, building on the legacy of the Bricks Parliamentary Forum, the Twelfth Forum aims
to foster consensus-based dialogue through four high-level sessions based on resilience,
innovation, cooperation and sustainability.
The deliberations will also cover issues related to terrorism.
In the 139th episode of Monkey Bath, Prime Minister Modi noted that the year 2023
was celebrated as the International Year of Millets at India's call.
The Prime Minister underlined that the initiative received a very positive response globally
and also provided an opportunity to the citizens to discover how deeply militias are rooted
in the country's own culture.
Mr Modi also spoke about a village called Kanduli in the West Jainthia Hills District
of Meghalaya where militias have been an integral part of food culture over many
generations.
The Prime Minister also talked about checking Zangma, a local farmer in the village of Saadolpada
from West Garohils district of Meghalaya.
He noted that these examples demonstrate how India's youth are linking traditional crops
with new opportunities and how villages are advancing on the path to prosperity while
preserving their heritage.
The Bhartiya Janata Party BJP is holding nationwide protests at all its state headquarters today
against Congress President Malik Arjan Khargay for allegedly making remarks about Prime Minister
Narendra Modi's late father, meanwhile Union Home Minister and senior BJP leader Amit Shah
has hit out at the Congress President over his alleged remarks about Prime Minister
Modi's father.
In a social media post, Mr Shah said this is not the first time that the Congress
party has used abusive language against the family of Prime Minister Modi.
A special MP-MLA court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh, today acquitted Congress leader Rahul
Gandhi in a defamation case over alleged remarks against Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who
was the BJP president at the time.
The case was filed in 2018 by local BJP leader Vijay Mishra over Gandhi's statement
at a campaign rally in Bengaluru.

Welcome back to the midday news.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi today congratulated Brazilian President Lula da Silva on his re-election
victory in a social media post. Prime Minister Modi said he looks forward to working closely
with the Brazilian president to further deepen and expand the multifaceted Indo-Brazil strategic partnership.
Leftist President Luiz Inácio Lulada Silva defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's intense presidential race.
Incumbent Lula won the final run-off election with 51% of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots.
Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 per cent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million
ballots.
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Arbanandas Sonawal is currently on a four-day
visit to South Korea, pitching India's maritime opportunity to the Korean industry.
In an official statement, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said, the
visit coincides with efforts by two countries to expand shipbuilding cooperation and
move India towards its goal of becoming one of the world's top five shipbuilding nations
Sonowal started the trip in Busan, which he referred to as the hub of Korea's maritime
industry, and interacted with Indian professionals working in Korean shipbuilding.
The Minister said India requires shipbuilders, marine engineers, naval architects, designers,
welders, project managers and technology specialists in plenty.
The Intermetrological Department, IMD, has said the deep depression over East-Central
and adjoining South-East Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm Ornab.
IMD informed that the Cyclonic Storm lay centered over East-Central and adjoining West-Central
Bay of Bengal, about 590 km northwest of Sri Vijayapuram in the Andhraban Islands
and 650 km east-south-east of Ishakapatnam today.
It also said the cyclonic storm is very likely to move north-westwards and intensify further
into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by midnight tonight.
Odisha has stepped up its preparedness as Cyclone Ornob over the Bay of Bengal moves
towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Southern Odisha is likely to experience heavy to extremely heavy rainfall as the
system intensifies ahead of its expected landfall on October 28.
The state government has mobilized disaster response teams and strengthened evacuation
arrangements to protect people in vulnerable districts.
We have more from our correspondent.
Orissa is bracing for the impact of Cyclone Arnab with Ganjam, Gajapati, Kurapur, Malkangiri
and Nabranpur among the key districts being closely monitored.
Kalahandin, Vapada and Kandhmal may also experience adverse weather.
The state government has intensified preparedness, arranging to shift around 3,000 pregnant
and women, two hospitals and making cyclone shelters and temporary evacuation centers operational.
Eight NDRF teams and 40 O'Draff teams have reportedly been deployed at strategic locations.
Eight ministers, including the Deputy Chief Ministers of the State Cabinet, have been
assigned responsibility for eight districts likely to be badly affected by very heavy
rainfall.
The India Meteorological Department forecasts that the cyclone will intensify into a severe
and subsequently a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh
coast on Wednesday.
The weather system over Bay of Bengal is now 580 km away from Gopalpur in Odisha.
The Odisha government has urged people in vulnerable areas to follow official advisories
and cooperate with evacuation measures.
Prakash Das, for Akaspani News, Bhubaneswar.
In Andhra Pradesh, IMD has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several coastal
districts on Tuesday and Wednesday.
IMD also warned of a possible rise in sea levels in low-lying coastal areas.
The Andhra Pradesh government has stepped up precautionary measures.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain on high alert, coordinate emergency operations and issue regular public warnings.
10 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams have been kept ready for rescue and relief work.
President R. P. Murmur, Vice-President S. P. Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have extended greetings to citizens on the occasion of Maharshi Valmiki Jayanti today.
In a social media post, the president said everyone effortlessly receives teachings on
duty, good conduct, selfless action, the welfare of others, friendship, sacrifice, righteousness
and devotion from the epic Ramayana composed by Maharishi Valmiki.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the noble thoughts of Maharishi Valmiki have been
the foundational elements of Indian culture and heritage which will continue to nurture
and flourish in the nation in every era.
A revered sage, a timeless epic and a remarkable journey of transformation, Valmiki Jayanti
celebrates the birth anniversary of Maharishi Valmiki, the revered author of Ramayana, fondly
known as Adhikavi or the first poet of Sanskrit literature.
According to tradition, Valmiki was once known as Ratnakar, whose life changed after
an encounter with Narad Muni.
Through deep meditation and devotion to Lord Ram, he transformed into a sage whose wisdom
continues to inspire generations.
Celebrated with prayers and grand precessions,
Valmiki Jayanthi reminds us that transformation is always possible
and that wisdom, compassion and devotion can shape not just a life,
but the destiny of humanity.
Shri Gyasa Pandey, Akashwani News, Delhi.
Vigilance Awareness Week is being observed across the country
from today till the first of next months to promote
property in public life and achieve a corruption-free society.
It is observed to create greater sensitivity about the need for
ethics and transparency in governance and public administration.
This year, Vigilance Awareness Week is celebrated under the theme,
Probity for Prosperity.
President of the Murmur Vice President Sipiratha Krishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi
have extended greetings for the success of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026.
President Murmur in her message noted that the theme highlights the importance of integrity
and honesty in promoting good governance and building a prosperous nation.
Global crude oil prices declined by more than 1% today after surging to their highest
levels in almost six months.
Brent Crude was trading 1.1% down at $115.41 per barrel.
West Texas Intermediate Crude was trading 1.6% lower at $101.62 per barrel at the
time of writing this report.
Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading in the positive zone in the afternoon
session today.
